rationale: The MIN(NEI, NEI − Δche) construction correctly implements "issued but not stockpiled" and the equity-channel decomposition of the archive's strongest signal (Post-Capex External Rescue) is a legitimate attribution test, though it is a narrow recombination of two existing archive legs and unlikely to add much beyond them.

The debt-channel counterpart is a coherent and symmetric attribution test, but the reasoning misstates the algebra — MIN(D, D − Δche) equals D − max(0, Δche) and does not "require positive debt financing," so heavy net repayers will populate the short leg and dilute the intended interpretation.

Replacing SUMRANK with MIN is a genuine change in conjunction logic (AND rather than average) that is properly motivated by the diagnosed failure of the earlier cash-burn sequencing signal, though the prior version's near-zero fmb_tstat makes the upside modest.

This is a cosmetic variant of the archive's "Equity-Deleveraging Investment Stretch" — the identical MIN(net equity, dltr) financing leg with IND_RANK(level) swapped for TS_RANK(own-cycle) on the investment leg — and it also overlaps "Equity-Timed Investment Peak," so it tests no substantively new mechanism.

Pairing the lagged inventory-acceleration event with the equity-in/debt-out financing leg is a new combination with a plausible working-capital-distress story and internally consistent sign, though both component legs are already archived and the sequencing lag may thin an already event-like signal.

This merely substitutes Δ(ppent/at) for (capx+aqc)/at in the archive's "Equity-Timed Investment Peak" while keeping the identical TS_RANK×TS_RANK structure, and TS_RANK of a first difference over five annual observations is a noisy proxy that does not constitute a substantive mechanism change.
